data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 and SRC_002 both fail to supply a causal mechanism, but SRC_003's shuffled-checklist design has a distinct mechanism defect: it treats robustness to shuffling as evidence of reliability independent of the checklist, yet its own counterconditions concede that panelists may ignore an obviously wrong shuffled checklist or that the checklist may function as a memory aid rather than a decision rule. Under either condition, non-degradation under shuffling is produced by panelists discarding the checklist, not by genuine reliability; the target provides no mechanism to distinguish checklist-rejecting noncompliance from competence. The shuffled-checklist manipulation thus confounds two causal pathways to the same observable (no accuracy degradation), so within a single evaluation it cannot isolate genuine reliability from strategic disregard of an implausible checklist.
